1.meaning: Say! — a command to speak or declare; the singular imperative addressed to one person.
1.grammar: Imperative (command) verb addressed to a single male/person: 'Say!'. From a hollow root, the middle weak letter drops in the command, leaving the short form 'qul'. The bare ending (no vowel) is characteristic of this singular imperative.

2.meaning: It has been revealed / inspired — divine communication has been sent down or conveyed (to someone). A passive verb: the focus is on the message being given, with the Giver understood rather than named.
2.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) passive verb (form IV). The opening vowelling marks it as passive ('it was/has been done to it'), and the ending denotes a third-person masculine singular subject — the thing revealed. Being passive, the doer (the Revealer) is left unstated. The long u of the prefix is formed by the damma plus the waw; the bare stem consonant carries -hi-.
2.root: و-ح-ى (w-h-y) — revelation, divine inspiration, conveying a message

3.meaning: 'To me / toward me.' It joins the preposition ilā, meaning 'to / toward,' with an attached first-person 'me,' expressing motion or direction toward the speaker.
3.grammar: A preposition meaning 'to / toward' with the attached pronoun 'me.' The base preposition is ilā, ending in a long vowel (written with alif maqsūra, ى). When the 'me' pronoun attaches, that final long vowel turns into yāʾ and merges with the pronoun's yāʾ, giving a doubled, stressed -ayya — the whole word reading ilayya, 'to me.'

4.meaning: 'That it (is) …' The emphasizing particle 'anna' ('that … indeed') with an attached 'it/he,' used to introduce a firmly asserted statement and tie it to a preceding verb such as 'know' or 'say.'
4.grammar: The particle anna ('that, indeed') with the attached pronoun -hu ('it/he,' masculine singular) as its subject. Anna introduces a strongly affirmed noun-clause ('that it is indeed…') and places its subject in the accusative; it commonly follows verbs of knowing, saying, or believing.

5.meaning: He listened — gave deliberate, attentive ear to something. This is the Form VIII (reflexive) counterpart of simply hearing: not sound merely reaching the ear, but a person turning toward it and taking it in on purpose.

parts.en: connecting hamza (hamzat waṣl) with its helping vowel, letting this verb pattern begin; it is dropped when the word follows a vowel in connected speech
the root s-m-ʿ 'hear' shaped by the Form VIII -t- infix: 'listen for oneself, give ear'

5.grammar: A completed-action (past tense) verb, third person masculine singular: 'he listened'. The final -a fatḥa is the standard past-tense marker for 'he'. The -t- slipped in after the first root letter is the mark of Form VIII, which typically adds the sense of doing something for oneself, with effort or attention. Because the stem itself begins with a vowelless consonant, the word needs the connecting hamza and its i- vowel to be pronounceable at the start of speech.

6.meaning: A small band or company of people — classically a group of men numbering roughly three to ten, a party that comes forward together.

parts.en: band, company, small party of people

6.grammar: A singular noun (collective in sense), indefinite. The -un ending is two things at once: the -u is the nominative case, which typically marks the doer of a verb or the subject of a sentence; the extra -n sound (nunation) marks the word as indefinite — 'a band', not 'the band'.
6.root: ن-ف-ر (n-f-r) — to go forth, rush out, shy away

7.meaning: From, out of, of — a preposition marking a starting point, origin, or source, or singling part out of a whole. Its core sense is movement or derivation away from a point.
7.grammar: A preposition. Its base form is min; the final vowel appears as -a (mina) when it is followed by a word beginning with the definite article 'al-', to ease pronunciation. It causes the following noun to take the genitive case.

8.meaning: A noun meaning 'the jinn' — a class of unseen beings created from smokeless fire, possessing free will and accountability like humankind.
8.grammar: A definite noun with the article al- ('the'). The -i (genitive) ending typically appears after a preposition or links the word to a preceding noun in a possessive 'of' relationship.
8.root: ج-ن-ن (j-n-n) — to cover, conceal, be hidden from sight

9.meaning: '…so / then they said.' Combines the connector 'so/then' (showing result or sequence) with a past-tense verb of speaking, third person plural — a completed act of saying by a group.
9.grammar: A completed-action (past) verb prefixed with 'fa-' ('so/then'), which links it to what precedes as a result or next step. The '-ū' ending (with silent trailing alif) marks the subject as 'they' (masculine plural).

10.meaning: A two-part expression: an emphatic particle that strongly affirms and confirms a statement ('truly, indeed, certainly'), fused with the attached pronoun 'we.' Together: 'truly we…' / 'indeed we…'
10.grammar: The particle inna gives strong emphasis and certainty to the clause it opens. The attached -ā is the pronoun 'we,' serving as the subject being emphasized: 'truly we…'

11.meaning: A past-tense verb meaning 'we heard / we listened' — the act of perceiving sound or a message, often carrying the further nuance of heeding or taking in what was said.
11.grammar: A completed (past-tense) verb. The attached ending -nā marks the subject as 'we', so the action is something a group did and finished: 'we heard'.

12.meaning: A recitation, a reading; a text meant to be recited aloud. As a common noun it denotes 'something recited,' and as a proper name it is the Qur'an, the recited Scripture.
12.grammar: A verbal noun meaning 'recitation.' The ending -an is accusative with nunation (the -n marking it indefinite, 'a recitation'); the accusative is the case typically marking the object of a verb or a noun being specified.

13.meaning: Something astonishing, a marvel or cause for wonder — an event or thing so strange that it provokes amazement or disbelief.
13.grammar: A singular indefinite noun. The '-an' ending (written with the doubled fatḥa, tanwīn) marks the accusative case for an indefinite noun — it commonly signals the object of a verb or the predicate after verbs of being ('was a wonder').

1.meaning: 'He/it guides, leads, shows the way'. The verb means to direct someone toward a goal or along a right path — to lead aright.
1.grammar: A third-person masculine singular present-tense verb. The ya- prefix marks a 'he/it' subject, and the final long -ī carries the sense 'he guides'. (This verb takes an object directly, 'guides someone', without needing 'to'.)
1.root: ه-د-ي (h-d-y) — to guide, lead aright, show the way

2.meaning: 'To / toward / up to' — a preposition marking the endpoint, goal, or limit of an action or motion: the direction something moves toward or the boundary at which it stops.
2.grammar: An invariable preposition. It has no case ending of its own but puts the noun that follows it into the genitive ('of / to' state). It indicates direction toward, or the terminal limit of, something.

3.meaning: right guidance, sound judgment, maturity of conduct; the state of being rightly directed and acting with good sense. It denotes integrity and correct, mature discernment as opposed to error and folly.
3.grammar: A definite verbal noun (the 'l-' is 'the'; its 'l' assimilates into the following 'r'). The -i ending is genitive: it typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… OF …') or follows a preposition.
3.root: ر-ش-د (r-sh-d) — to be rightly guided, to follow the right course

4.meaning: 'So we believed / we had faith' — the act of coming to faith, trusting, and affirming the truth, attributed to a 'we' subject, introduced by a connective 'so/then'.

parts.en: so / then (connective showing result or sequence)

4.grammar: A prefixed connective fa- ('so/then') on a Form IV perfect (completed-action) verb. The suffix -nā marks the subject as 'we' and the perfect form indicates a completed act ('we believed / have believed').
4.root: أ-م-ن (ʾ-m-n) — to be safe, secure; to trust, believe

5.meaning: 'with it,' 'by it,' 'by means of it' — the instrumental/accompaniment preposition 'with/by' joined to 'it' (referring to a masculine singular thing). It marks the means or instrument through which something is done.
5.grammar: A preposition ('with/by') joined to the attached pronoun '-hi' ('it/him'), referring back to a masculine singular thing. The pronoun takes the '-i' vowel form ('hi') because it follows a word ending in an '-i' sound, marking it as the object of the preposition: 'by means of it.'

6.meaning: A two-part expression combining 'and' with the particle of emphatic future negation. The core particle 'lan' negates a coming action with finality: 'will never / shall not (ever).' It denies that something will happen in the future, often with a tone of absolute impossibility.
6.grammar: A conjunction 'wa' ('and') joined to the negating particle 'lan'. 'Lan' governs a following present-tense verb, putting it into the subjunctive mood and turning its meaning into an emphatic denial of the future: 'it will never happen.'

7.meaning: A verb meaning 'we associate / set up partners' — to make something a partner or associate of another (especially associating partners with Allah). The verb pattern conveys deliberately joining one thing to another as an equal.
7.grammar: A present-tense verb of the causative pattern (Form IV), built without any doubled root letter. The nu- prefix marks the doers as 'we' (first person plural). The stem-final -a (subjunctive mood) is the form taken after certain particles, such as those meaning 'that' or 'it is not for us to …'.

8.meaning: In/with our Lord. 'Rabb' has no single English equivalent: it is the Master and Owner who also nurtures, sustains, raises up and brings to completion whatever He owns — authority and loving upbringing joined in one word.

parts.en: genitive ending required after the preposition

8.grammar: Preposition + noun + attached possessive pronoun. The -i ending is genitive: a word takes it when it follows a preposition (as after bi-) or when it is linked to a preceding noun in an 'X of Y' relation. The suffix -nā attached to a noun always means 'our'.
8.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to own, master, nurture and bring to maturity

9.meaning: Anyone / a single one: 'one' used to mean a sole individual, especially in negative or conditional contexts ('not anyone', 'any single person').
9.grammar: A noun meaning 'one / a single one', frequently used for 'anyone' when paired with a negation. The final -an (nunation) marks it as indefinite and in the accusative case, the case typically used for a verb's object.

1.meaning: And that … — a connecting 'and' plus the emphatic particle anna ('that / indeed') with the attached pronoun 'he/it.' anna introduces and stresses a statement, like saying 'and (the fact) that he/it is …'
1.grammar: A particle combination. wa- is 'and.' anna is an emphatic conjunction meaning 'that' (it introduces a noun-clause and gives it the force of 'indeed'). The attached -hu is its subject pronoun, 'he/it.' anna requires the following noun to be in the accusative case.

2.meaning: An expression meaning 'He is exalted / supremely high'. Said of Allah, it declares that He is far above and transcendently beyond any deficiency, partner, or comparison. It functions as a phrase of glorification.
2.grammar: A perfect (past-form) verb, 3rd person masculine singular, used to affirm an established quality: 'He is exalted, high above'. This is a defective verb (its final root letter is weak), so the stem ends in a long -ā standing in for that weak letter, not a case marker. It is built on Form VI of the root meaning 'high/lofty'.
2.root: ع-ل-و (ʿ-l-w) — height, loftiness, to be high

3.meaning: Majesty, grandeur, exalted greatness — the loftiness and sublime dignity of the one described. The word also carries in ordinary Arabic the senses of good fortune and of 'grandfather', all from a root idea of what is weighty and eminent.
3.grammar: A noun in the nominative: the -u ending typically marks the subject of a sentence or the thing being spoken about. There is no -n (nunation) after the -u; a bare -u like this signals that the word is bound to a following possessor — 'the majesty OF …'.
3.root: ج-د-د (j-d-d) — to be great, weighty, serious

4.meaning: Our Lord, Master, and Sustainer: the One who owns, governs, nurtures, and brings to completion. Rabb combines ownership, authority, and loving cultivation of what He sustains; the '-our' joins the speakers to Him as those under His care.
4.grammar: The noun rabb ('Lord, Master, Sustainer') with the attached possessive pronoun -nā ('our'). The -i before the pronoun is the genitive case, used after a preposition, after a calling/oath, or to link the word to a preceding noun in an 'of' relationship.
4.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, sustain, master, own

5.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
5.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

6.meaning: A verb meaning 'he took (for himself), adopted, or acquired' — to take something and make it one's own; from a reflexive pattern implying taking to oneself.
6.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) Form VIII verb, third-person masculine singular ('he took'). Form VIII often carries a reflexive sense (taking for oneself). The final -a is the standard perfect ending, marking a completed act. The initial alif is a connecting hamza, sounded only at the start of an utterance.

7.meaning: A female companion — a woman who accompanies a man as his consort or wife. Literally 'one who keeps company with', so it stresses the bond of companionship rather than a legal contract.

parts.en: feminine ending: makes it a female companion

7.grammar: An active participle (a 'doer' noun) made feminine by the -at ending. The final -an is the accusative case plus nunation: the -a typically marks the direct object of a verb (the thing acted upon), and the -n marks the word as indefinite — 'a female companion', not 'the'.

8.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
8.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

9.meaning: The noun 'child, son, or offspring' — what is born of someone; can denote a son specifically or progeny generally.
9.grammar: A masculine noun with the ending '-an' (tanwīn), the indefinite accusative — the case typical of a direct object ('a child' as the thing taken/had). The final alif is the spelling support for this '-an' ending.
9.root: و-ل-د (w-l-d) — to beget, give birth; child, offspring

1.meaning: And that … — a connecting 'and' plus the emphatic particle anna ('that / indeed') with the attached pronoun 'he/it.' anna introduces and stresses a statement, like saying 'and (the fact) that he/it is …'
1.grammar: A particle combination. wa- is 'and.' anna is an emphatic conjunction meaning 'that' (it introduces a noun-clause and gives it the force of 'indeed'). The attached -hu is its subject pronoun, 'he/it.' anna requires the following noun to be in the accusative case.

2.meaning: He/it was, or there was — the past tense of the verb 'to be', expressing that something existed or used to be the case.

parts.en: to be, was, used to be

2.grammar: A past-tense verb (a 'hollow' verb of being), third-person masculine singular ('he/it was'). The final '-a' marks the ordinary past tense for 'he/it'. Paired with a following present-tense verb, it often conveys 'used to' do something.

3.meaning: 'He says' or 'he is saying' — the act of speaking or uttering words. The imperfect tense conveys an ongoing, habitual, or present/future action.
3.grammar: Imperfect (present/future) verb, third person masculine singular. The ya- prefix marks 'he', the stem qūl carries the meaning 'say', and the final -u is the indicative ending, signalling a plain factual statement (as opposed to a subjunctive -a or jussive sukūn used after certain particles).

4.meaning: Our foolish one. 'Safīh' is not merely unintelligent: it names someone light-minded and reckless, lacking sound judgement, who speaks or acts without weighing consequences — moral and mental foolishness together.
4.grammar: A descriptive noun/adjective on the faʿīl pattern with an attached possessive pronoun. The -u ending is nominative, the case typically used for the doer of a verb or the subject being described. The suffix -nā on a noun means 'our', so the word describes someone belonging to the speakers' own group.
4.root: س-ف-ه (s-f-h) — to be light-minded, foolish, lacking sound judgement

5.meaning: 'To / before / upon' — a preposition whose core sense is being on top of, above, or directed onto something; with a verb of presenting it carries the directional sense 'to / before / in front of,' and it can also convey obligation ('incumbent upon').
5.grammar: A preposition. Its basic meaning is 'on, upon, over,' but with verbs of displaying or presenting it shades into 'to / before / in front of.' It governs the following noun in the genitive case. It is fixed in form and takes no changing ending of its own (its final long -ā is an unchanging part of the word).
5.root: — (preposition; loosely related to the sense of 'height/elevation')

6.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
6.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

7.meaning: Gross excess — a statement or act that overshoots all bounds; something outrageous, extravagant, wildly wide of the truth. The root pictures going far away from the mark.
7.grammar: A verbal noun, indefinite. The -an ending combines the accusative -a with nunation -n. The accusative typically marks the direct object of a verb, or an adverbial specification answering 'in what way?' or 'as what?'; the nunation shows the word is indefinite.
7.root: ش-ط-ط (sh-ṭ-ṭ) — to go far off, exceed all bounds

1.meaning: 'And that we …' — a connector plus the emphatic particle 'anna', which introduces a reported statement ('that …') while affirming it strongly, with the attached pronoun 'we' as its subject.

parts.en: anna — 'that', the particle introducing a reported clause, with emphasis
we — the pronoun -nā, whose n merges into the doubled n of anna, so only the long ā is written

1.grammar: Connecting particle + emphatic particle + attached pronoun. 'Anna' places the noun or pronoun that follows it in the accusative, and the attached pronoun 'we' fills that slot as its subject, giving 'that we …'. Because the pronoun's n runs into the doubled n of anna, the written form shows the doubled n followed only by the long -ā.

2.meaning: We thought, supposed, were of the opinion. 'Ẓann' covers the whole range from bare conjecture and suspicion up to strong presumption — belief held short of certain knowledge.

parts.en: the root ẓ-n-n: to think, suppose, presume
we (past-tense subject ending; its n merges with the root's final n)

2.grammar: A completed-action (past tense) verb with the subject built into the ending: -nā attached to a past verb always means 'we' did it. The doubled n comes from the last root letter n meeting the n of the -nā ending. This verb characteristically takes a whole clause as its content — 'we supposed that …'.
2.root: ظ-ن-ن (ẓ-n-n) — to suppose, conjecture, believe without certainty

3.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
3.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'

4.meaning: A particle of strong negation directed at the future: 'never; will not at all.' It emphatically denies that something will ever happen and puts the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive.
4.grammar: A negating particle that governs a following present-tense verb, denying it for the future and forcing that verb into the subjunctive mood (so the verb takes a final '-a' instead of '-u'). It has no ending of its own.

5.meaning: '(That) you would say' / 'you say' — an act of speaking or uttering words, performed by a single male addressee.
5.grammar: A present/future-tense verb. The ta- prefix marks the doer as 'you' (singular masculine). The final -a ending (subjunctive) is the form used after particles like 'that,' 'so that,' or 'lest,' signalling a dependent or anticipated action rather than a plain statement.

6.meaning: Humankind; human beings collectively, viewed as the species. It denotes people in general, often paired in contrast with the unseen world.
6.grammar: The article al- means 'the' (here generic, denoting the whole class). The -u ending is nominative: it typically marks the word as the doer or subject of a sentence.
6.root: ا-ن-س (ʾ-n-s) — to be sociable, familiar, human

7.meaning: 'And the jinn' — a class of unseen beings created from fire, possessing free will and accountability, who normally exist beyond ordinary human perception.
7.grammar: The prefix wa- means 'and'. The article al- means 'the'. The -u ending is nominative: it typically marks the word as the doer or subject of a sentence. The root sense of 'concealment' fits these beings who are hidden from sight.

8.meaning: 'To / before / upon' — a preposition whose core sense is being on top of, above, or directed onto something; with a verb of presenting it carries the directional sense 'to / before / in front of,' and it can also convey obligation ('incumbent upon').
8.grammar: A preposition. Its basic meaning is 'on, upon, over,' but with verbs of displaying or presenting it shades into 'to / before / in front of.' It governs the following noun in the genitive case. It is fixed in form and takes no changing ending of its own (its final long -ā is an unchanging part of the word).
8.root: — (preposition; loosely related to the sense of 'height/elevation')

9.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
9.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

10.meaning: A noun meaning 'a lie / falsehood' — a deliberately false statement, an untruth fabricated against the truth.
10.grammar: An indefinite noun ('a lie') with the accusative -an ending (tanwīn). The accusative commonly marks the object of a verb (e.g. fabricating a lie); the -an tanwīn shows it is indefinite.
10.root: ك-ذ-ب (k-dh-b) — to lie, to declare false

1.meaning: And that … — a connecting 'and' plus the emphatic particle anna ('that / indeed') with the attached pronoun 'he/it.' anna introduces and stresses a statement, like saying 'and (the fact) that he/it is …'
1.grammar: A particle combination. wa- is 'and.' anna is an emphatic conjunction meaning 'that' (it introduces a noun-clause and gives it the force of 'indeed'). The attached -hu is its subject pronoun, 'he/it.' anna requires the following noun to be in the accusative case.

2.meaning: He/it was, or there was — the past tense of the verb 'to be', expressing that something existed or used to be the case.

parts.en: to be, was, used to be

2.grammar: A past-tense verb (a 'hollow' verb of being), third-person masculine singular ('he/it was'). The final '-a' marks the ordinary past tense for 'he/it'. Paired with a following present-tense verb, it often conveys 'used to' do something.

3.meaning: Men: adult male human beings. The plural noun denotes men as a group, sometimes carrying the sense of people of standing or strength.
3.grammar: A masculine plural noun (the plural of rajul, 'a man'). The -un ending is the nominative case with nunation, marking it as indefinite — 'men' rather than 'the men.'
3.root: ر-ج-ل (r-j-l) — man, manhood; also foot/on foot

4.meaning: From, out of, of — a preposition marking a starting point, origin, or source, or singling part out of a whole. Its core sense is movement or derivation away from a point.
4.grammar: A preposition. Its base form is min; the final vowel appears as -a (mina) when it is followed by a word beginning with the definite article 'al-', to ease pronunciation. It causes the following noun to take the genitive case.

5.meaning: A noun with the definite article, meaning 'the mankind / humans / human beings' as a collective. The word evokes humans in their sociable, companionable nature, as opposed to hidden, unseen beings.
5.grammar: al- is the definite article 'the'. The -i ending is genitive: it typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… of mankind') or follows a preposition. The collective noun ins refers to humankind as a whole.
5.root: ء-ن-س (ʾ-n-s) — familiarity, sociability (humans as social beings)

6.meaning: They seek refuge, take shelter, put themselves under someone's protection — clinging to a protector out of fear of harm.

parts.en: present-tense prefix for a third-person subject

6.grammar: An ongoing-action (present/future) verb, third person masculine plural. The ya- prefix signals a third-person subject; the -ū ending makes it 'they' (masculine plural). The final -na is the indicative marker: it shows the verb stands as a plain statement of fact, and it would drop away after particles that make a verb subjunctive or jussive.
6.root: ع-و-ذ (ʿ-w-dh) — to seek refuge, take shelter with

7.meaning: In/with men — 'rijāl' is the plural of 'rajul', an adult male, a man in full standing.
7.grammar: Preposition + broken (internal) plural noun. The -in ending is the genitive case (-i) plus nunation (-n): the genitive is required after a preposition such as bi-, and it also appears when a noun is linked to a preceding noun as 'X of Y'; the nunation marks the noun as indefinite — 'men', not 'the men'.
7.root: ر-ج-ل (r-j-l) — foot, walking; hence the adult male who goes on foot

8.meaning: From, out of, of — a preposition marking a starting point, origin, or source, or singling part out of a whole. Its core sense is movement or derivation away from a point.
8.grammar: A preposition. Its base form is min; the final vowel appears as -a (mina) when it is followed by a word beginning with the definite article 'al-', to ease pronunciation. It causes the following noun to take the genitive case.

9.meaning: A noun meaning 'the jinn' — a class of unseen beings created from smokeless fire, possessing free will and accountability like humankind.
9.grammar: A definite noun with the article al- ('the'). The -i (genitive) ending typically appears after a preposition or links the word to a preceding noun in a possessive 'of' relationship.
9.root: ج-ن-ن (j-n-n) — to cover, conceal, be hidden from sight

10.meaning: So they increased them — they added to them, made them grow in some respect. The verb can take two objects: to increase someone in something.
10.grammar: Connector + completed-action (past) verb + object pronoun. The -ū ending on a past verb means 'they' (masculine plural) did it; the attached -hum is the object, 'them'. The prefix fa- links what follows as an immediate or consequent result, unlike plain 'and'. The middle root letter y surfaces as the long ā of the stem, the normal change in hollow verbs.

11.meaning: Oppressive burden — being overtaken and weighed down; the word carries the senses of exhaustion, humiliation, insolent overreach and sin, all from a root meaning to catch up with and overwhelm someone.
11.grammar: A verbal noun, indefinite. The -an ending is the accusative -a plus nunation -n: the accusative typically marks a direct object, or a specification answering 'in what respect?' (as with a verb meaning 'to increase someone IN something'); the -n shows the word is indefinite.

1.meaning: 'And that they…' — the connector 'wa-' ('and') joined to 'anna' ('that, indeed') and the pronoun 'they,' introducing a further affirmed clause.
1.grammar: Begins with 'wa-' ('and'). Built on the particle 'anna' ('that…, indeed'), which introduces and affirms a clause and puts its noun into the accusative. The attached '-hum' is the pronoun 'they/them' for a male-inclusive group.

2.meaning: They thought, supposed, presumed — held an opinion falling short of certain knowledge, ranging from mere suspicion to firm assumption.
2.grammar: A completed-action (past) verb, third person masculine plural. The -ū ending built into the verb means 'they' (masculine plural) did it; the silent alif written after the wāw is a spelling convention only and is not pronounced. The verb typically governs a whole clause as the content of the thought.
2.root: ظ-ن-ن (ẓ-n-n) — to suppose, conjecture, believe without certainty

3.meaning: 'Just as / in the same way that' — a phrase of comparison joining 'like / as' to 'what', meaning 'like that which...' or 'in the manner that...'.
3.grammar: The comparison particle ka- ('like / as') joined to mā ('what / that which'). Together they introduce a likeness or manner — 'just as...', 'in the same way that...' — comparing one thing or action to another.

4.meaning: You (plural) thought / you assumed — past tense, 2nd person plural: the belief or assumption held by those being addressed. In context, refers to the false assumption that the Prophet would not return from Hudaybiyyah.

parts.en: you (pl.) thought / assumed (2nd masc. pl. past)

4.grammar: Past tense verb, 2nd person masculine plural, Form I. A doubled root (ظ-ن-ن) with assimilation of the doubled nūn.
4.root: ظ-ن-ن (ẓ-n-n) — to think, to assume; often with a sense of conjecture or false belief

5.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
5.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'

6.meaning: A particle of strong negation directed at the future: 'never; will not at all.' It emphatically denies that something will ever happen and puts the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive.
6.grammar: A negating particle that governs a following present-tense verb, denying it for the future and forcing that verb into the subjunctive mood (so the verb takes a final '-a' instead of '-u'). It has no ending of its own.

7.meaning: That He raise up, rouse, or send forth — to stir something into action and dispatch it, or to raise the dead to life.
7.grammar: Present-tense verb. The ya- prefix marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he'); the final -a is the subjunctive mood, the form used after particles like 'that' or 'so that' to express purpose or a dependent action.
7.root: ب-ع-ث (b-ʿ-th) — to raise up, rouse, send forth

8.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
8.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

9.meaning: Anyone / a single one: 'one' used to mean a sole individual, especially in negative or conditional contexts ('not anyone', 'any single person').
9.grammar: A noun meaning 'one / a single one', frequently used for 'anyone' when paired with a negation. The final -an (nunation) marks it as indefinite and in the accusative case, the case typically used for a verb's object.

1.meaning: 'And that we …' — a connector plus the emphatic particle 'anna', which introduces a reported statement ('that …') while affirming it strongly, with the attached pronoun 'we' as its subject.

parts.en: anna — 'that', the particle introducing a reported clause, with emphasis
we — the pronoun -nā, whose n merges into the doubled n of anna, so only the long ā is written

1.grammar: Connecting particle + emphatic particle + attached pronoun. 'Anna' places the noun or pronoun that follows it in the accusative, and the attached pronoun 'we' fills that slot as its subject, giving 'that we …'. Because the pronoun's n runs into the doubled n of anna, the written form shows the doubled n followed only by the long -ā.

2.meaning: We touched, felt for, probed — reached out to find something by feeling, hence also 'we sought out, tried to reach'.

parts.en: touched, felt for, sought by groping (root l-m-s)

2.grammar: A completed-action (past) verb with the subject in its ending: -nā attached to a past verb always means 'we' performed the action. The a-a vowelling of the stem (la-mas-) is the plain, basic (Form I) verb pattern, with no added prefixes or doubling.
2.root: ل-م-س (l-m-s) — to touch, feel, grope for

3.meaning: The sky or heaven — all that rises and spreads overhead: the visible canopy above and the heights beyond it. A definite noun with the article 'al-', so 'the sky / the heaven'.
3.grammar: A definite noun (with 'al-', here assimilated to 'as-samāʾ'). The final '-a' ending is accusative: it typically marks the word as the object of a verb — the thing an action is done to — or the item being mentioned after certain particles.
3.root: س-م-و (s-m-w) — to be high, lofty; that which is elevated overhead

4.meaning: So we found it / we found her — 'wajada' means to come upon something, to discover it to be in a certain state, and by extension to experience or feel it.
4.grammar: Connector + completed-action (past) verb + object pronoun. The -nā ending means 'we' did the finding; the attached -hā is the object and refers back to something grammatically feminine, so it renders as 'it' or 'her'. The prefix fa- marks what follows as the immediate outcome of what came before.
4.root: و-ج-د (w-j-d) — to find, come upon, experience

5.meaning: It was filled — a passive verb: something was made full, packed with whatever fills it, with the filler's identity left unstated.

parts.en: was filled — the root m-l-ʾ 'fill' in its passive vowelling

5.grammar: A completed-action (past) verb in the passive voice. The passive is shown purely by the vowels: u on the first letter and i on the second (mu-li-) instead of the active ma-la-, and it means the doer is not named. The -at ending marks a third-person feminine singular subject — 'it (feminine) was filled'.

6.meaning: Guards — a body of watchmen set to protect and keep watch. The word is collective, naming the whole guard rather than one guard.
6.grammar: A collective noun, indefinite. The -an ending is the accusative -a plus nunation -n: the accusative typically marks the direct object of a verb or a specification answering 'with what?' / 'in what respect?'; the -n shows the noun is indefinite.

7.meaning: 'Severe / intense / harsh.' An adjective describing something strong, forceful, and hard to bear.
7.grammar: An adjective in an intensive pattern ('very strong/severe'). The -an ending marks it as indefinite and in the accusative case, the form used when it describes a noun that is itself indefinite and accusative.
7.root: ش-د-د (sh-d-d) — to be strong, intense, severe

8.meaning: And blazing flames — 'shuhub' is the plural of 'shihāb', a burning brand, a flame, and especially a shooting star or meteor streaking through the sky.
8.grammar: Connector + broken (internal) plural noun, indefinite. The plural is formed by reshaping the vowels inside the word rather than adding a suffix. The -an ending is the accusative -a plus nunation -n: the accusative typically marks a direct object or a specification, and the -n marks the word as indefinite.
8.root: ش-ه-ب (sh-h-b) — blaze, flame; a mingling of white with black as of fire

1.meaning: 'And that we …' — a connector plus the emphatic particle 'anna', which introduces a reported statement ('that …') while affirming it strongly, with the attached pronoun 'we' as its subject.

parts.en: anna — 'that', the particle introducing a reported clause, with emphasis
we — the pronoun -nā, whose n merges into the doubled n of anna, so only the long ā is written

1.grammar: Connecting particle + emphatic particle + attached pronoun. 'Anna' places the noun or pronoun that follows it in the accusative, and the attached pronoun 'we' fills that slot as its subject, giving 'that we …'. Because the pronoun's n runs into the doubled n of anna, the written form shows the doubled n followed only by the long -ā.

2.meaning: 'We were' — the past tense of the verb 'to be,' establishing a past state or condition for a group including the speaker. It is the basic verb of existence and of 'being something.'
2.grammar: The past tense of 'to be' in the first-person plural ('we were'). The subject suffix is -nā ('we'); its nūn is written with a shadda (نَّ) because it merges with the final nūn of the verb stem kun-, and the alif spells the long -ā. A hollow verb, its middle weak letter drops in this form. It sets up a past state, and what follows describes how 'we' were.
2.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — to be, to come into being, existence

3.meaning: We sit, we take up a seated position — and by extension we settle down, stay put, station ourselves somewhere or hold back from moving.

parts.en: sit, settle, take a position (root q-ʿ-d)

3.grammar: An ongoing-action (present/future) verb, first person plural. The na- prefix means 'we' are the ones acting. The final -u is the indicative ending: it marks the verb as a plain statement of fact; after particles that make a verb subjunctive it would become -a, and after jussive particles the ending would be dropped entirely.
3.root: ق-ع-د (q-ʿ-d) — to sit, settle, remain in place

4.meaning: A two-part word: the preposition 'min' ('from / out of / some of') joined to the pronoun 'it' (feminine). Together: 'from it / out of it / of it,' indicating a source or a portion taken from a feminine thing.
4.grammar: A preposition 'min' with the attached pronoun '-hā' ('it/her'), referring to a feminine noun. 'Min' indicates origin, source, or a part taken from a whole; the attached pronoun is in the object form required after a preposition.

5.meaning: "Stations / seats / positions" — places where one sits or is posted; battle stations or assigned positions.
5.grammar: A plural noun of place ('places of sitting/posting'). The -a ending is the accusative case, typically marking the direct object of a verb. As a 'diptote' broken plural it takes a single -a (no tanwīn). It is the plural of 'maqʿad' (a seat or station).
5.root: ق-ع-د (q-ʿ-d) — to sit, a seat, a station/position

6.meaning: For hearing / for listening. 'Samʿ' is the faculty of hearing and the act of it — the ear's taking in of sound, and by extension paying heed.

parts.en: for, in order to (purpose or attachment)
the (definite article; its connecting hamza drops after li-)
hearing, listening — the article's l assimilates into the s, shown by the doubling mark
genitive ending required after the preposition

6.grammar: Preposition + definite article + verbal noun. The -i ending is genitive, the case a noun takes after a preposition such as li-, or when linked to a preceding noun as 'X of Y'. The prefix li- commonly expresses purpose ('for the sake of, in order to') or belonging. Because s is a 'sun letter', the l of the article is written but not pronounced, doubling the s instead.

7.meaning: A compound meaning 'then whoever' or 'so whoever'. It combines 'then/so' with the conditional/relative 'who', introducing whatever person meets a stated condition.
7.grammar: The connector fa- ('then/so', often answering or following a condition) joined to man ('whoever / the one who'), which refers to people and introduces a condition: 'whoever does X…'. man does not change its ending; the clause after it supplies the rest of the meaning.

8.meaning: He listens attentively, gives ear — the Form VIII (reflexive) counterpart of merely hearing: turning deliberately toward a sound and taking it in.

parts.en: listen attentively — root s-m-ʿ with the -t- infix of Form VIII
helping vowel added at the end

8.grammar: An ongoing-action verb, third person masculine singular ('he'), in its jussive (shortened) shape — the form used after conditional or jussive particles, whose base ending is a bare consonant (yastamiʿ) rather than -u. The -i heard at the end is not a case or mood marker but a helping vowel supplied so that two vowelless consonants do not collide with what follows.

9.meaning: Now — the present moment, this very time, as opposed to past or future.

parts.en: the definite article, inseparable from this word; its opening hamza is a connecting hamza (hamzat waṣl), sounded as 'a' only when speech begins here and elided after a preceding vowel, leaving just l-

9.grammar: A time noun that is fixed (indeclinable): its final -a never changes for case, unlike ordinary nouns that swap between -u, -a and -i. It functions adverbially, answering 'when?' — 'at the present moment'. The definite article is part of the word and is not detachable, and because its hamza is a connecting hamza the word is voiced 'l-āna' whenever it follows a vowel in continuous speech, and 'al-āna' only when spoken in isolation or at the start of an utterance.
9.root: — (no productive verbal root; some link it to أ-و-ن ʾ-w-n, 'time, period')

10.meaning: He finds or obtains — to come upon, to have available, to possess the means for something.
10.grammar: A present-tense verb in the jussive mood. The ya- prefix marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he/it'). The cut-short ending (a vowelless final consonant, -jid rather than -jidu) shows the jussive mood, typically triggered by a preceding particle of negation or condition such as 'does not' or 'whoever'.
10.root: و-ج-د (w-j-d) — to find, to come upon, to experience, to exist

11.meaning: For him / to him / belonging to him. A small preposition meaning 'to/for' joined to the pronoun 'him', expressing possession, benefit, or direction toward him.
11.grammar: A preposition 'li-' ('to/for') fused with the attached pronoun 'him'. The pronoun 'him' stays the same; it is the preposition that changes, its vowel shifting from -i (li-) to -a (la-) when an attached pronoun follows it directly. The whole unit commonly conveys possession or that something is for someone's benefit.

12.meaning: A blazing flame — a burning brand or firebrand, and especially a shooting star or meteor blazing across the sky.
12.grammar: A singular noun, indefinite. The -an ending is the accusative -a plus nunation -n: the accusative typically marks the direct object of a verb or a specification answering 'as what?'; the -n marks the noun as indefinite — 'a flame', not 'the flame'.

13.meaning: A watcher, sentinel, or lookout — someone (or a whole party) stationed to observe and lie in wait; by extension the act of close watching or ambush. It carries the sense of vigilant surveillance kept over something, whether protective or predatory.
13.grammar: A noun, indefinite (no 'the'). The -an ending (tanwīn fatḥ) is the accusative: it marks a word as the object of a verb, or as a descriptive/adverbial complement telling how or in what capacity something is — 'as a watcher', 'by way of watching'.
13.root: ر-ص-د (r-ṣ-d) — to watch, observe, lie in wait

1.meaning: 'And that we …' — a connector plus the emphatic particle 'anna', which introduces a reported statement ('that …') while affirming it strongly, with the attached pronoun 'we' as its subject.

parts.en: anna — 'that', the particle introducing a reported clause, with emphasis
we — the pronoun -nā, whose n merges into the doubled n of anna, so only the long ā is written

1.grammar: Connecting particle + emphatic particle + attached pronoun. 'Anna' places the noun or pronoun that follows it in the accusative, and the attached pronoun 'we' fills that slot as its subject, giving 'that we …'. Because the pronoun's n runs into the doubled n of anna, the written form shows the doubled n followed only by the long -ā.

2.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
2.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

3.meaning: 'We know / we are aware' — from a verb meaning to perceive, realise, or have an inkling of something, often used of knowledge one arrives at by noticing clues. It is regularly used in expressions of not knowing, i.e. having no way to tell.
3.grammar: A present-tense verb. The na- prefix means the doer is 'we'. The stem ends in a long -ī because the root's final letter is a weak yā'; this long -ī is the ordinary present-tense (indicative) form of such verbs, and it stays unchanged in a plain statement or a simple negation.
3.root: د-ر-ي (d-r-y) — to perceive, come to know

4.meaning: 'Is it evil…? / whether harm…' — the word for evil, harm, or badness, prefixed by a question-marker. Sharr is the broad opposite of khayr (good): anything injurious, corrupt, or bringing hurt.
4.grammar: A noun carrying the interrogative hamza. The a- prefix turns what follows into a question ('is it…?') and, after verbs of knowing, into an indirect 'whether'. The -un ending (tanwīn ḍamm) is the nominative, the case used for the subject of a sentence or for what is being asserted about it.

5.meaning: 'It was intended / willed / meant' — a passive verb: someone purposed or aimed at a thing, but the one doing the intending is deliberately left unnamed. The underlying verb means to want, will, or set one's purpose toward something.

parts.en: causative (form IV) prefix, vowelled for the passive

5.grammar: A completed-action (past) verb in the passive voice, third person masculine singular. The final -a is the ordinary past-tense ending for 'he/it did'. The u–i vowel pattern (u- on the prefix, i in the stem) is what makes it passive: 'it was intended' rather than 'he intended', with no agent stated. The middle root letter is a weak wāw, which surfaces here as the long -ī of the stem.
5.root: ر-و-د (r-w-d) — to seek, aim at, desire

6.meaning: 'With / about whom,' or 'than who.' It combines the preposition bi- ('with, by, about') with the relative/interrogative 'who,' referring to a person or persons — 'the one(s) who.'
6.grammar: The preposition bi- ('with/about') joined to man ('who'). The word man does not change its ending for case; it can act as a question word ('who?') or as a relative word ('the one who'), and bi- supplies the sense 'with/about whom.'

7.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
7.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

8.meaning: The earth; the land, ground, or soil. The world we walk upon, as opposed to the sky.
8.grammar: A feminine singular noun with the definite article al- ('the'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('... of the earth') or follows a preposition (as after 'in / on the earth').

9.meaning: A connective particle meaning 'or', specifically the 'or' that pairs with a preceding question to offer an alternative ('…or…?'). It links two possibilities being weighed against each other, often after an opening interrogative.

parts.en: or (in alternatives, esp. after a question)

9.grammar: An indeclinable particle (no case or tense ending). It typically introduces the second branch of a two-part question or a balanced alternative, presenting the two as equally consequential.

10.meaning: A verb meaning 'he intended', 'he willed', or 'he meant' — to direct one's purpose toward something, to want or aim at it.
10.grammar: Past-tense (perfect) verb, third-person masculine singular ('he'), in the derived (form IV) pattern arāda. The bare stem with a final -a denotes a completed action by a single male subject, with the sense of actively willing or purposing something.
10.root: ر-و-د (r-w-d) — to seek, want, aim at

11.meaning: An expression meaning 'at them' or 'with them' — the preposition 'bi' (with, by, at) joined to the pronoun 'them' (a group). The exact shade ('at/by/with them') depends on the verb it accompanies.
11.grammar: A preposition (bi-, 'with/by/at') with the attached pronoun -him ('them,' for a group of males). The pronoun is in the genitive, the case always required after a preposition.

12.meaning: 'Their Lord' — the noun 'Lord' (Master, Sustainer, Nurturer who owns, provides, and brings to maturity) joined to the pronoun 'their'.
12.grammar: A noun with a possessive pronoun. The -u vowel before -hum is the nominative ending, typically marking the word as the subject/doer. The suffix -hum means 'their', referring to a masculine plural group.
12.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to be lord, master, to nurture and sustain

13.meaning: Right guidance, sound direction, maturity of judgment — being on a straight and correct course, the opposite of error or folly.
13.grammar: A masculine noun. The -an ending is the accusative with 'tanwīn' (the doubled-fatḥa nunation), which generally marks a word as an object of a verb, or as an adverbial/specifying complement ('... in the way of right guidance'). The tanwīn signals the noun is indefinite ('right guidance' in general).
13.root: ر-ش-د (r-sh-d) — right guidance, sound judgment, maturity

parts.en: anna — 'that', the particle introducing a reported clause, with emphasis
we — the pronoun -nā, whose n merges into the doubled n of anna, so only the long ā is written

2.meaning: "from us" — the preposition 'from' (indicating origin, source, or starting point) fused with the attached pronoun 'us'. It can also carry a partitive sense, 'some of us / a part of us'.
2.grammar: A preposition with an attached object pronoun. The base 'min' normally takes a vowelless final consonant, but before the pronoun '-nā' the nūn is doubled (assimilation), giving 'minnā'. The suffix '-nā' is the first-person plural object/possessive pronoun meaning 'us' or 'our'.
2.root: — (preposition; the pronoun has no triliteral root)

3.meaning: Those who are righteous, morally upright, and sound in conduct — people whose deeds are good and who set things right. As a plural noun it denotes the class of virtuous, godly people collectively.
3.grammar: An active participle ('one who is righteous / does good') made definite by the prefix al- ('the'). The -ūna ending marks a sound masculine plural in the nominative case — the form typically used when such a plural is the subject of a sentence ('the righteous ones [are/do] …').

4.meaning: 'And among us / and some of us' — a linking 'and' joined to the preposition min, which expresses 'from', 'out of', 'part of', or 'belonging to a group', with 'us' attached. It commonly introduces a portion of a larger whole.
4.grammar: A connective plus a preposition with an attached pronoun. The final -nā is the pronoun 'us'; because it begins with n, it merges with the n of min and is written with a doubling mark. Words following min stand in the genitive, though attached pronouns like -nā show no case ending of their own.

5.meaning: An adverb/preposition meaning 'apart from, other than, short of, below.' It points to something falling outside or beneath a named thing — 'aside from X' or 'lesser than X'.
5.grammar: An invariable adverbial noun used like a preposition. It carries a fixed -a ending and governs a following noun in the genitive, yielding the sense 'other than …' or 'short of …'.
5.root: د-و-ن (d-w-n) — to be below, lesser, or beneath

6.meaning: A demonstrative pronoun meaning 'that' — pointing to something regarded as distant or elevated, as opposed to 'this' (hadha) for what is near. It singles out a masculine singular thing and lends it a sense of distinction or loftiness.
6.grammar: A demonstrative for a masculine singular referent at a distance. The -ka ending is an address particle directed at a single male listener; it does not change for case. The whole word stays fixed in form regardless of its grammatical position.

7.meaning: 'We were' — the past tense of the verb 'to be,' establishing a past state or condition for a group including the speaker. It is the basic verb of existence and of 'being something.'
7.grammar: The past tense of 'to be' in the first-person plural ('we were'). The subject suffix is -nā ('we'); its nūn is written with a shadda (نَّ) because it merges with the final nūn of the verb stem kun-, and the alif spells the long -ā. A hollow verb, its middle weak letter drops in this form. It sets up a past state, and what follows describes how 'we' were.
7.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — to be, to come into being, existence

8.meaning: Paths, ways, or layered tracts — the plural of ṭarīqa, a way or course; classically also understood of layered heavens, each a 'track' one above another.
8.grammar: A 'broken' plural of ṭarīqa ('way, path'). This plural pattern is a diptote: it never takes nunation, and it shows a single -a vowel for both the accusative and the genitive cases (only -u would mark the nominative). The -a here is thus its case ending; in a diptote, an accusative reading (e.g. as the object of a verb) and a genitive reading look identical.

9.meaning: Separate strips, divided parties, disparate factions — the plural of qiddah, literally a length cut off from a whole, hence groups split off along different lines, each following its own way. It pictures unity sliced into differing sects or dispositions.
9.grammar: A plural noun, indefinite. The -an ending (tanwīn fatḥ) is the accusative, the case for a verb's object and, very often, for a descriptive complement stating the condition or shape something is in — 'as separate groups'.
9.root: ق-د-د (q-d-d) — to cut lengthwise, split into strips

2.meaning: We thought, supposed, were of the opinion. 'Ẓann' covers the whole range from bare conjecture and suspicion up to strong presumption — belief held short of certain knowledge.

parts.en: the root ẓ-n-n: to think, suppose, presume
we (past-tense subject ending; its n merges with the root's final n)

2.grammar: A completed-action (past tense) verb with the subject built into the ending: -nā attached to a past verb always means 'we' did it. The doubled n comes from the last root letter n meeting the n of the -nā ending. This verb characteristically takes a whole clause as its content — 'we supposed that …'.
2.root: ظ-ن-ن (ẓ-n-n) — to suppose, conjecture, believe without certainty

3.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
3.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'

4.meaning: A particle of strong negation directed at the future: 'never; will not at all.' It emphatically denies that something will ever happen and puts the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive.
4.grammar: A negating particle that governs a following present-tense verb, denying it for the future and forcing that verb into the subjunctive mood (so the verb takes a final '-a' instead of '-u'). It has no ending of its own.

5.meaning: 'We frustrate / render powerless / escape beyond reach' — to make another party unable to achieve their aim, whether by thwarting them or by slipping away so they cannot lay hold of one. It is built on the idea of reducing someone to incapacity.
5.grammar: A present-tense causative (form IV) verb. The nu- prefix means the doers are 'we' (its u vowel marks the causative pattern 'to make X incapable'). The final -a is the subjunctive ending, used after particles such as an ('that'), lan ('never will'), and li- ('so that'); it presents the action as dependent or hypothetical rather than as a flat statement of fact.

6.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
6.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

7.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
7.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

8.meaning: The earth; the land, ground, or soil. The world we walk upon, as opposed to the sky.
8.grammar: A feminine singular noun with the definite article al- ('the'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('... of the earth') or follows a preposition (as after 'in / on the earth').

9.meaning: A two-part expression combining 'and' with the particle of emphatic future negation. The core particle 'lan' negates a coming action with finality: 'will never / shall not (ever).' It denies that something will happen in the future, often with a tone of absolute impossibility.
9.grammar: A conjunction 'wa' ('and') joined to the negating particle 'lan'. 'Lan' governs a following present-tense verb, putting it into the subjunctive mood and turning its meaning into an emphatic denial of the future: 'it will never happen.'

10.meaning: 'We frustrate Him / escape beyond His reach' — to render someone unable to accomplish His purpose, or to elude His grasp entirely. The verb combines thwarting with getting away.
10.grammar: A present-tense causative (form IV) verb with an attached object pronoun. The nu- prefix means 'we'; the -a before the pronoun is the subjunctive ending, used after particles like an, lan, and li- to mark a dependent or hypothetical action. The final -hu is the object pronoun 'him'; the small superscript wāw is a recitation sign showing that its vowel is drawn out.

11.meaning: Flight, fleeing, running away — the verbal noun of 'to flee'; the act itself of escaping from something feared or pursued.
11.grammar: A verbal noun (the name of an action), indefinite. The -an ending (tanwīn fatḥ) is the accusative; on a verbal noun of this kind it typically works adverbially, telling in what manner something is done — 'by fleeing', 'in flight'.

1.meaning: 'And that we …' — a connector plus the emphatic particle 'anna', which introduces a reported statement ('that …') while affirming it strongly, with the attached pronoun 'we' as its subject.

parts.en: anna — 'that', the particle introducing a reported clause, with emphasis
we — the pronoun -nā, whose n merges into the doubled n of anna, so only the long ā is written

1.grammar: Connecting particle + emphatic particle + attached pronoun. 'Anna' places the noun or pronoun that follows it in the accusative, and the attached pronoun 'we' fills that slot as its subject, giving 'that we …'. Because the pronoun's n runs into the doubled n of anna, the written form shows the doubled n followed only by the long -ā.

2.meaning: A particle meaning 'when' or 'at the point that' something occurred — pointing to the moment a past event took place and often implying that one thing happened upon the completion of another. In other uses it can carry the sense of 'not yet'.
2.grammar: A particle (a small connecting word), not a noun or verb, so it has no case or tense ending. It introduces a clause and links it in time to another event — most often 'when / as soon as' a past action happened.

3.meaning: A past-tense verb meaning 'we heard / we listened' — the act of perceiving sound or a message, often carrying the further nuance of heeding or taking in what was said.
3.grammar: A completed (past-tense) verb. The attached ending -nā marks the subject as 'we', so the action is something a group did and finished: 'we heard'.

4.meaning: The guidance — being shown the right way and led along it. Hudā is not merely information but direction that actually brings one to the goal: right guidance as a gift, the opposite of straying.
4.grammar: A definite noun: the al- prefix means 'the', marking it as a known, specific thing. The word ends in alif maqṣūra (a long -ā), a fixed ending — such nouns do not change form for the nominative, accusative, or genitive, so the case must be judged from context rather than from the ending. The wavy maddah sign written over that final alif is a recitation mark only: it signals that the long vowel is stretched because a word beginning with hamza follows. That hamza is the opening letter of the next word and forms no part of this one, so the word itself is simply al- + hudā.

5.meaning: We have believed; we have come to faith and trust — to affirm belief, give one's trust, and feel secure in that conviction, stated by a group about themselves.
5.grammar: A past-tense verb on the form-IV pattern (āmana, 'to believe / to have faith'). The ending -nā (a single morpheme, نَا) attached to a past verb marks the subject as 'we'. The doubled 'n' heard in 'āmannā' comes from the verb stem's final 'n' meeting the 'n' that begins the -nā ending.

6.meaning: 'with it,' 'by it,' 'by means of it' — the instrumental/accompaniment preposition 'with/by' joined to 'it' (referring to a masculine singular thing). It marks the means or instrument through which something is done.
6.grammar: A preposition ('with/by') joined to the attached pronoun '-hi' ('it/him'), referring back to a masculine singular thing. The pronoun takes the '-i' vowel form ('hi') because it follows a word ending in an '-i' sound, marking it as the object of the preposition: 'by means of it.'

7.meaning: A compound meaning 'then whoever' or 'so whoever'. It combines 'then/so' with the conditional/relative 'who', introducing whatever person meets a stated condition.
7.grammar: The connector fa- ('then/so', often answering or following a condition) joined to man ('whoever / the one who'), which refers to people and introduces a condition: 'whoever does X…'. man does not change its ending; the clause after it supplies the rest of the meaning.

8.meaning: He believes, has faith, trusts and affirms as true — inwardly accepting and giving secure assent, the core act of faith.
8.grammar: A present-tense verb in the causative (Form IV, أَفْعَلَ) pattern. The yu- prefix means 'he'. The vowel-less final -n marks the jussive mood, the clipped form a verb takes after certain particles (such as negation or conditions) rather than the plain ongoing form.

9.meaning: 'In / with his Lord' — rabb means the master and owner who nurtures what He owns: the one who creates, sustains, raises up, provides for, and brings a thing to its completion, and who therefore has the right to command it. It is 'Lord' in the sense of caring authority, not merely a title of rank.
9.grammar: A preposition attached to a noun with a possessive pronoun. The -i ending is genitive, the case a noun always takes after a preposition and when it is possessed by a following word. The attached -hi means 'his'; its i-vowel is the form used after an i-vowel or -ī, as here. The small superscript yā' is a recitation sign showing the pronoun's vowel is drawn out.

10.meaning: A two-part word: the connective particle 'fa-' meaning 'so', 'then', or 'therefore' (drawing a consequence from what precedes), joined to 'lā', the particle of negation/prohibition. Together they convey 'so do not …' or 'so there is no …'.
10.grammar: 'fa-' is a connector that links a clause to what came before and often signals a result or consequence. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a present-tense verb it commonly forms a prohibition ('do not …') or a simple negation ('not'). It carries no ending of its own.

11.meaning: He fears, dreads, or is in awe of — an inner apprehension of harm, danger, or a dreaded outcome.
11.grammar: A present-tense verb. The ya- prefix indicates a third-person masculine singular subject ('he does …'). The final -u (ḍamma) marks the indicative mood, the plain factual form used for an action stated as ongoing or habitual.

12.meaning: A shortfall, deduction, or being short-changed — having what is due to one diminished or undervalued. It is the loss suffered when a reward or price is trimmed below its proper worth.
12.grammar: A noun, indefinite. The -an ending (tanwīn fatḥ) is the accusative, marking a word as the object of a verb — the sort of thing feared, suffered, or inflicted.

13.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
13.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

14.meaning: Oppressive burden — being overtaken and weighed down; the word carries the senses of exhaustion, humiliation, insolent overreach and sin, all from a root meaning to catch up with and overwhelm someone.
14.grammar: A verbal noun, indefinite. The -an ending is the accusative -a plus nunation -n: the accusative typically marks a direct object, or a specification answering 'in what respect?' (as with a verb meaning 'to increase someone IN something'); the -n shows the word is indefinite.

1.meaning: 'And that we …' — a connector plus the emphatic particle 'anna', which introduces a reported statement ('that …') while affirming it strongly, with the attached pronoun 'we' as its subject.

parts.en: anna — 'that', the particle introducing a reported clause, with emphasis
we — the pronoun -nā, whose n merges into the doubled n of anna, so only the long ā is written

1.grammar: Connecting particle + emphatic particle + attached pronoun. 'Anna' places the noun or pronoun that follows it in the accusative, and the attached pronoun 'we' fills that slot as its subject, giving 'that we …'. Because the pronoun's n runs into the doubled n of anna, the written form shows the doubled n followed only by the long -ā.

2.meaning: "from us" — the preposition 'from' (indicating origin, source, or starting point) fused with the attached pronoun 'us'. It can also carry a partitive sense, 'some of us / a part of us'.
2.grammar: A preposition with an attached object pronoun. The base 'min' normally takes a vowelless final consonant, but before the pronoun '-nā' the nūn is doubled (assimilation), giving 'minnā'. The suffix '-nā' is the first-person plural object/possessive pronoun meaning 'us' or 'our'.
2.root: — (preposition; the pronoun has no triliteral root)

3.meaning: Those who submit — people who hand themselves over wholly to Allah, entering His peace and safety by surrendering their will to His. The root joins the ideas of peace, wholeness, and safe delivery, so a muslim is one made whole by yielding.
3.grammar: A definite noun-adjective (an active participle of the causative pattern: 'one who does X'). The al- prefix means 'the'. The -ūna ending is the sound masculine plural in the nominative case — the case used for the subject of a sentence or for the word that completes 'X is …'. As an object or after a preposition it would appear as -īna instead.

4.meaning: 'And among us / and some of us' — a linking 'and' joined to the preposition min, which expresses 'from', 'out of', 'part of', or 'belonging to a group', with 'us' attached. It commonly introduces a portion of a larger whole.
4.grammar: A connective plus a preposition with an attached pronoun. The final -nā is the pronoun 'us'; because it begins with n, it merges with the n of min and is written with a doubling mark. Words following min stand in the genitive, though attached pronouns like -nā show no case ending of their own.

5.meaning: Those who swerve from justice — people who deviate from what is straight and right and so act unfairly. Notably, the root runs in two directions: the simple verb qasaṭa means to deviate and wrong, while its causative aqsaṭa means to act with equity, so this form denotes the unjust deviators.
5.grammar: A definite active participle ('the ones who do X') made plural. The al- prefix means 'the'. The -ūna ending is the sound masculine plural in the nominative, the case for the subject of a sentence or the completing word of 'X is …'; as an object or after a preposition it would read -īna.
5.root: ق-س-ط (q-s-ṭ) — to deviate / to deal equitably (opposed senses)

6.meaning: A compound meaning 'then whoever' or 'so whoever'. It combines 'then/so' with the conditional/relative 'who', introducing whatever person meets a stated condition.
6.grammar: The connector fa- ('then/so', often answering or following a condition) joined to man ('whoever / the one who'), which refers to people and introduces a condition: 'whoever does X…'. man does not change its ending; the clause after it supplies the rest of the meaning.

7.meaning: He submitted / surrendered (himself); he gave himself over wholly, devoting and resigning himself to Allah. The verb carries the sense of entering into peace and security by total surrender — the very root of the word 'Islam.'
7.grammar: A past-tense verb, 'he submitted,' describing a completed act by a single male (or 'one who'). The final -a is the standard ending of this third-person masculine singular past form. The four-letter (causative) pattern adds the sense of actively giving oneself up to something.
7.root: س-ل-م (s-l-m) — soundness, peace, safety; to submit/surrender

8.meaning: So those / then those are the ones — a connector 'so/then' joined to a demonstrative pointing to a distant or already-mentioned group: 'those people, they (are the ones who)…'.
8.grammar: 'fa-' is a connector meaning 'so/then', often introducing a result or consequence. 'ulā'ika' is a plural demonstrative ('those') pointing to people, typically picking up a previously described group and setting them up as the subject. It is fixed in form and does not change for case.

9.meaning: 'They sought out deliberately / aimed for the right thing' — to search purposefully for what is most fitting, correct, or worthy, taking pains to hit the mark rather than settling for the first thing found.

parts.en: seek out, aim at what is right

9.grammar: A completed-action (past) verb in the intensive self-directed pattern (form V), where the ta- prefix means the subject undertakes the action for or upon itself — 'to go about seeking'. The ending marks the doers as 'they' (masculine plural); because the root's last letter is a weak yā', the usual -ū plural ending appears as -aw, and the silent alif written after the wāw is a spelling convention, not a sound.
9.root: ح-ر-ي (ḥ-r-y) — to aim at, seek what is fitting

10.meaning: Right guidance, sound direction, maturity of judgment — being on a straight and correct course, the opposite of error or folly.
10.grammar: A masculine noun. The -an ending is the accusative with 'tanwīn' (the doubled-fatḥa nunation), which generally marks a word as an object of a verb, or as an adverbial/specifying complement ('... in the way of right guidance'). The tanwīn signals the noun is indefinite ('right guidance' in general).
10.root: ر-ش-د (r-sh-d) — right guidance, sound judgment, maturity

1.meaning: 'And as for …' A connective that introduces and sets apart a new topic for separate comment, usually anticipating a matching response clause. The 'and' joins it on; 'ammā' means 'as for (such-and-such)…'
1.grammar: The conjunction wa ('and') joined to the detailing/conditional particle ammā ('as for…'). Ammā singles out a topic for separate treatment and normally anticipates a matching clause (often introduced by 'fa-') that supplies the comment. Neither part takes case endings.

2.meaning: Those who swerve from justice — people who deviate from what is straight and right and so act unfairly. Notably, the root runs in two directions: the simple verb qasaṭa means to deviate and wrong, while its causative aqsaṭa means to act with equity, so this form denotes the unjust deviators.
2.grammar: A definite active participle ('the ones who do X') made plural. The al- prefix means 'the'. The -ūna ending is the sound masculine plural in the nominative, the case for the subject of a sentence or the completing word of 'X is …'; as an object or after a preposition it would read -īna.
2.root: ق-س-ط (q-s-ṭ) — to deviate / to deal equitably (opposed senses)

3.meaning: 'But / and they were / they used to be' — the past tense of the verb 'to be' in the third-person masculine plural. Beyond a simple 'they were', it commonly conveys a habitual, ongoing past state ('they used to').
3.grammar: The fa- prefix means 'and / so / but', linking to what precedes. The verb is the past tense of 'to be'; the -ū ending is the subject 'they' for a group of males (the written alif after it is silent). It states a past condition, often a customary one ('they were / used to be').
3.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — to be, exist, come to be

4.meaning: For Hell / to Hell — the prefix 'for/to' joined to Jahannam, the name of the fire of punishment in the next life.
4.grammar: 'For/to Hell.' The prefix li- means 'for' or 'to (the purpose of).' Jahannam is a proper name treated as not fully declinable, so after the preposition it takes the special -a ending in place of the usual genitive -i.

5.meaning: Firewood — gathered wood, kindling, fuel for a fire; also, figuratively, whatever is fed to a blaze.
5.grammar: A collective noun, indefinite. The -an ending (tanwīn fatḥ) is the accusative, used for a verb's object and for a complement stating what something serves as — 'as fuel'.

1.meaning: 'And that, if…' — a chain of small connecting words: 'and', plus the light particle an which introduces a reported or explanatory clause ('that…'), plus law, the 'if' used for suppositions, especially ones contrary to fact ('if such-and-such had been the case…').

parts.en: that (introducing a clause); its n assimilates into what follows
if (law), with the doubled l from that assimilation and a linking vowel

1.grammar: A cluster of particles, not a noun or verb, so it takes no case or tense. The n of an assimilates into the l of law, which is why the l is written doubled. The final -i is a helping vowel with no meaning of its own: Arabic avoids letting a vowelless consonant collide with the consonant cluster beginning the next word, so a short i is inserted to smooth the join.

2.meaning: 'They stood firm / were upright / kept straight' — a past-tense verb meaning to be or become straight and upright, to hold a steady, correct course, or to remain firmly committed, referring to a group of males (or a mixed group). The Form X pattern here carries the sense of standing oneself upright and steadfast.
2.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb in the Form X (is-ta-…) pattern, here meaning to make oneself upright / hold a straight course. The ending -ū means 'they', a group of males or a mixed group (third-person masculine plural). The final silent alif (-ū + ا) is just a spelling convention after this plural ending.
2.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand, rise, be upright

3.meaning: 'To / before / upon' — a preposition whose core sense is being on top of, above, or directed onto something; with a verb of presenting it carries the directional sense 'to / before / in front of,' and it can also convey obligation ('incumbent upon').
3.grammar: A preposition. Its basic meaning is 'on, upon, over,' but with verbs of displaying or presenting it shades into 'to / before / in front of.' It governs the following noun in the genitive case. It is fixed in form and takes no changing ending of its own (its final long -ā is an unchanging part of the word).
3.root: — (preposition; loosely related to the sense of 'height/elevation')

4.meaning: The way — a beaten path or road, and hence a manner, method, or course of conduct that one habitually follows. It suggests a route trodden until it is well marked.
4.grammar: A definite feminine noun. The al- prefix means 'the'; its l is absorbed into the following ṭ (a 'sun letter'), which is why the ṭ is doubled in pronunciation. The final -i vowel on the tā' marbūṭa is the genitive case: it marks the word as either governed by a preposition or possessed by a preceding noun ('the … OF the way').
4.root: ط-ر-ق (ṭ-r-q) — to beat a path, road, way

5.meaning: 'We would surely have given them water to drink' — the causative verb means to supply someone with drink, to water or irrigate them, prefixed by an emphatic 'surely'. It conveys granting drink as a provision, not merely handing over a cup.
5.grammar: A completed-action (past) verb in the causative pattern (form IV, 'to make someone drink'), with the emphatic lām prefixed. That la- both stresses the statement and is the standard opener for the result-clause of a supposition ('… we would surely have …'). The -nā ending is the past-tense subject 'we'; the stem's final weak letter appears as -ay before it. The closing -hum is the object pronoun 'them'.

6.meaning: Water — the liquid itself, and by extension any fluid or drink; a standing symbol of life and provision.
6.grammar: A noun, indefinite. The -an ending (tanwīn fatḥ) is the accusative, marking a word as the object of a verb — the thing given, made, or acted upon. The wavy sign over the alif is a recitation mark showing the long -ā is stretched before the hamza that closes the word.

7.meaning: Abundant, copious, plentiful — said above all of water that flows freely and without stint, more than enough.
